HomePage.title: Praja Ledger
HomePage.lede: A public register of Telangana leaders. Each line names the document it comes from.

Landing.headline: Know your leader's record before you vote.
Landing.lede: What is on record for the leaders compiled so far: what they have done, what was promised, and what they have been accused of. Each entry shows its source, and every case shows exactly how far it has gone.
Landing.searchPlaceholder: Search a leader or constituency, e.g. Kodangal
Landing.searchHint: Or open the leader list. Location is not used.
Landing.searchEmpty: No leader in this edition matches that.
Landing.closerTitle: Get closer to the people you elect, on the record.
Landing.closerLede: Follow your leaders, ask them questions in public and share what’s on record. Everything stays tied to sources, so a conversation never turns into a rumour.
Landing.followBody: Get an alert when a leader’s record changes: a case moves stage, a promise is updated, or their office posts an update.
Landing.askBody: Put a question to your MLA or MP. Others in the constituency back it, the leader’s office answers in public, and unanswered questions show how many days they’ve waited.
Landing.shareBody: Send any entry to WhatsApp or Instagram as a card with its source and date printed on it, plus a link to the live record.
Landing.rulesTitle: Built so no side can game it.
Landing.rulesLede: Every party gets the same fields, the same source rules and the same moderation. No party funding, no ads, no rankings.
Landing.legendNote: Solid for official records, outline for reports, dashed for claims.
Landing.ruleSourceBody: Court orders, audits and affidavits link to the document. Anything unconfirmed is marked Verify.
Landing.ruleCaseTitle: An allegation is not a conviction
Landing.ruleCaseBody: Cases show their exact stage, from allegation to verdict. The site never calls anyone guilty.
Landing.ruleReplyBody: A verified office can attach a reply to any entry about them. We publish it unedited, next to the entry.
Landing.ruleCommunityBody: Phone-verified accounts, comments reviewed before they appear, and no comments on legal cases.
Landing.comingNext: Coming next: alerts, office replies and accounts.
Landing.stepsTitle: How a question reaches your leader
Landing.step1Body: One clear question about a promise, a project or a local issue, addressed to your MLA or MP.
Landing.step2Body: Voters in the same constituency add “Me too”. Duplicates are merged so one question carries the weight.
Landing.step3Body: Every question passing a set number of backers goes to the leader’s verified office each week.
Landing.step4Body: The answer appears on the leader’s page. No answer? The question stays up, showing how long it has waited.
Landing.startBody: 119 assembly seats and 17 Lok Sabha seats. This edition has a record for {count} leaders. The rest are not compiled yet.
Landing.formulaDetail: A news report says the allegation is that ₹55 cr was diverted. A chargesheet was filed in March 2026. Charges are not yet framed. This is not a conviction.
Landing.rythuDetail: The Socio-Economic Outlook 2026 says ₹8,744.13 cr was paid to 69.40 lakh pattadars from 16 to 24 Jun 2025.
Landing.rythuGap: Deccan Chronicle reported on 23 Apr 2026 that a further ₹3,446 cr was still needed for farmers above 2 acres. No later document confirms that payment.
Landing.houseDetail: The same outlook says 3,24,536 houses are sanctioned against a target of 4,50,000, and 2,62,449 are under construction. It does not say how many families have moved in.
Landing.weekRule: One recent change per party, newest first.

about.office: The office held now, and earlier offices, from a government, legislature, or election record.
about.education: Education and profession from the election affidavit.
about.income: Income-tax totals for each of the last five financial years, for the member, and for spouse and dependants as one group, from the election affidavit, with the PDF page.
about.assets: Movable assets, immovable assets, and liabilities, for the member and for spouse and dependants as one group, labelled with the affidavit year and PDF page. Property is usually valued at purchase price, not market value.
about.affidavitChange: A change calculated only from two linked affidavits. The line shows both figures and the formula, and is labelled Calculated by Praja Ledger.
about.estimates: A later figure only from a named published source, such as a minister’s annual asset declaration or a court or Enforcement Directorate attachment order. Labelled Estimate by that source.
about.cases: Each case in the affidavit: FIR number, police station, sections, court, and whether charges are framed, with its stage.
about.legislature: Questions, bills, and attendance from PRS Legislative Research for an MP, or from the Telangana Legislature for an MLA.
about.constituency: Works in the constituency, including MPLADS for an MP, from the official list.
about.minister: Schemes run as minister, with the budget and the outcome numbers from an official document.
about.business: Company directorships from Ministry of Corporate Affairs records. A government contract to a linked firm only with a court, audit, or news report.
about.conduct: Public statements and allegations about conduct, each with its source and its stage.

CasesPage.title: Legal cases

Manifestos.title: Manifestos
Manifestos.description: Telangana manifesto promises, each on its own page, with a status count only where the list is frozen and the party is in government.
Manifestos.intro: Each manifesto is listed on its own. A tally is the count of promises in each status, plus the total.
Manifestos.notCompiled: Not compiled yet. The promise list is not frozen, so there is no tally.
Manifestos.pdfMissing: The manifesto PDF was not opened. No promise text is invented here, and there is no tally.

Manifestos.context: Opened sources that do not state this measure
Manifestos.audit: A government count is not an independent audit.

Manifestos.cardSource: Sources are named on each promise. As of 25 Oct 2026.

MethodManifesto.title: Manifesto statuses
MethodManifesto.intro: A manifesto promise uses one of six statuses. The tally is how many promises are in each status, plus the total. It is not a share of the total, a grade, or one combined number. Parties are not ranked, and two parties’ tallies are not shown side by side.
MethodManifesto.delivered: Delivered as promised. A sourced figure meets the sourced target.
MethodManifesto.partial: Delivered in part. A sourced outcome is lower, narrower, or later than the promised target.
MethodManifesto.progress: In progress. A source says the work is underway and the target is not yet met.
MethodManifesto.notStarted: Not started. A source says the work has not begun.
MethodManifesto.dropped: Dropped or reversed. A source says the promise was withdrawn or undone.
MethodManifesto.unverified: Can't be verified. The outcome source is missing, or the opened sources do not state the measure the promise uses.
MethodManifesto.ruleFrozen: A tally is shown only when the promise list is frozen and that manifesto’s party is in government. The Congress 2023 list was frozen on 25 Oct 2026. The manifesto PDF was not opened, so each quote is not compiled yet.
MethodManifesto.ruleEmpty: BRS 2014, BRS 2018, and BJP promises specific to Telangana are not frozen, because those documents were not opened. Those pages do not show a tally. BRS 2023 and the BJP 2023 state manifesto are promises made by parties that are not in government. They do not show a tally.
MethodManifesto.ruleMonth: Month of the term is counted from the swearing-in date to 25 Oct 2026. It does not use the clock on the reader’s device. Congress was sworn in on 7 Dec 2023. Month 1 starts that day. Each next month starts on the same day of the month. 25 Oct 2026 falls in month 35 of a 60-month term.
MethodManifesto.ruleGap: A gap sentence is written only when both numbers come from an opened source. A quote is the sentence in the manifesto PDF, with its page. A news paraphrase is not entered as a quote.
MethodManifesto.ruleClaim: A rival-party document is shown as that party’s claim. It is not written as this site’s finding.
MethodManifesto.freezeCongress: Congress 2023: frozen on 25 Oct 2026. Quotes are not compiled yet.
MethodManifesto.freezeBjpUnion: BJP promises for Telangana, against the Union government: not frozen.
MethodManifesto.freezeBrs2023: BRS 2023: not in government. The list is not frozen.
MethodManifesto.freezeBjp2023: BJP 2023 state manifesto: not in government. The list is not frozen.

ConstituenciesPage.title: Constituencies
ConstituenciesPage.description: Telangana’s 119 Assembly seats and 17 Lok Sabha seats, with the sitting member named from an opened source.
ConstituenciesPage.intro: 119 Assembly seats and 17 Lok Sabha seats. The member is named only where this edition has opened a source. A dossier exists only for leaders already in the book.

SeatPage.rupeesNote: Rupees, as printed on the affidavit.
SeatPage.acNote: The sitting member is the name on the Telangana Legislative Assembly member list, read 25 Oct 2026. The constituency number and the reservation category come from the Election Commission’s 2023 detailed results. (SC) and (ST) are marked on the constituency name in that report. The Commission’s highlight counts 88 General, 19 Scheduled Caste and 12 Scheduled Tribe seats, so an unmarked seat is General.
SeatPage.pcNote: The member is the winning candidate named by the Election Commission for this seat in the June 2024 Lok Sabha result. The same name is on the Telangana government’s Lok Sabha list. The reservation category for these 17 seats is not compiled yet.

FinancesPage.title: State finances
FinancesPage.description: Telangana budget estimates for 2026–27, public debt at 31 March 2025, and outstanding guarantees.
FinancesPage.intro: These figures are kept apart. The budget estimate is a plan for 2026–27. The public-debt stock is what the annexure said was owed on 31 March 2025. Outstanding liabilities are a wider percentage of GSDP, and guarantees sit outside that percentage. A December 2025 total, reported from a government document, is in the records below. It is not that March 2025 stock.
FinancesPage.budgetNote: A minus sign is a revenue deficit. PRS says the large borrowing and repayment in 2024–25 include Rs 1,29,376 crore of short-term advances from the RBI, and the repayment of those advances. The 2026–27 fiscal deficit is 3% of GSDP. The revenue surplus that year is estimated at 0.3% of GSDP.
FinancesPage.debtNote: Do not add this stock to the 28.7% liability estimate. They are different measures, taken at different dates.

CorrectionsPage.title: Corrections
CorrectionsPage.description: How to suggest a correction, and how a leader's office can reply to a line.
CorrectionsPage.intro: A suggestion names the record, says what is wrong, and points to a public document. It stays in the queue until a reviewer links it to the change that fixed it, or declines it with a note. The contact email is not published.
CorrectionsPage.emailNote: The email is for a follow-up. It is not shown on the public register, and it is removed 90 days after a decision.
CorrectionsPage.notConfigured: This form is not accepting submissions yet. The server is missing its bot check.
CorrectionsPage.replyEmailNote: The office email is checked and then kept off the public page. A signed letter can be used instead.
CorrectionsPage.needId: The record id, such as PL-C-01.
CorrectionsPage.needSentence: The sentence that is wrong, copied as it stands.
CorrectionsPage.needDocument: A public document that says otherwise: a judgment, an Election Commission table, a budget paper, or a named news report of one of those.
CorrectionsPage.rumour: A rumour, a slogan, or a post without a document does not correct a line.

MethodPage.title: How we record
MethodPage.description: The rules Praja Ledger uses before a line about a Telangana leader is written down.
MethodPage.intro: Praja Ledger writes down what a public document already says about a Telangana leader, an election, a scheme, or the state’s accounts. The checked date on every page is the day those documents were read for this edition.
MethodPage.earnsBody: A line has to be checkable. The usual documents are an Election Commission report, a paper of the state government, a budget analysis that cites those papers, or a news report that names the court date, the order, or the person who said the thing.
MethodPage.statusBody: Pending means a court date or an unfinished payment is still open. A discharge is written only as the news report described it, until the order is opened. A discharge is not a conviction. An estimate is a budget number, not money already spent.
MethodPage.outBody: Speeches that are not tied to a count. Social-media claims. Anything attributed only to “sources.” A chargesheet rewritten as if the trial had ended. A percentage turned into a rupee figure the source did not print. Leaders who hold office but have no separate line yet. This edition leaves out most ministers and most MLAs for that reason.
MethodPage.numbersBody: Scheme counts are the government’s unless a line names another publisher. Debt figures say which measure they are, because public debt, outstanding liabilities, and guarantees are not the same pile of money. Party names follow the document being quoted. The Commission’s assembly report writes BHRS for Bharat Rashtra Samithi.
MethodPage.notBody: It is not the Government of Telangana. It is not a court, and it is not legal advice. Reading a line here is not a finding of guilt or of innocence.

DataPage.title: Open data
DataPage.description: Download the public register as JSON or CSV, and check a nightly snapshot with sha256sum.
DataPage.intro: These files are the public register. They leave out contact emails, drafts, and unpublished rows.
DataPage.verifyBody: Save hashes.txt in a folder. Save each snapshot in a snapshots folder beside it, using the file name from the table. In that folder, run sha256sum. A matching line means the file is the published snapshot.
DataPage.notConfigured: Snapshot hashes are not available from this server yet.
